topics.title: WHAT IS A DATABASE? / WHAT IS A DBMS?

questions.prompt: What are a collection of book data and the software managing it called, respectively?
options: Query and query result
Database and DBMS
DBMS and database
Schema and instance
questions.explanation: The database is the data, while the DBMS is the software that manages it. The two terms should not be reversed.

questions.prompt: Which component sits between applications and data to manage access?
options: A database instance
An individual query
The DBMS
A schema describing the data
questions.explanation: The DBMS coordinates interactions with the data; a record or report is itself data.

questions.prompt: Which collection best represents a library database?
options: Only a Books schema, with no data instance
Only the program implementing borrowing and returns
Only an SQL query that has not been executed
An organised collection of related books and loans
questions.explanation: A database models part of the real world. The interface and program code are not the library’s collection of data.

questions.prompt: How does adding a new book differ from generating a list of current loans?
options: One changes the data, while the other reads a result
One changes the schema, while the other changes the physical layout
Both only read existing data
Both necessarily change the table schema
questions.explanation: Adding a record changes the instance. Producing a list can be a read-only query and does not require a schema change.

questions.prompt: Which statement about a DBMS and a relational database is correct?
options: A query result is the entire DBMS
A DBMS is software and is not synonymous with a table
Database and DBMS are two names for the same instance
A schema is all the software that manages a database
questions.explanation: Management software can serve many tables. A table is a data object, not the software managing it.

questions.prompt: Which DBMS layer chooses between an index access path and a table scan?
options: Buffer management
Query planning
Disk-space allocation
Record compaction
questions.explanation: Query planning selects the physical access path; buffer and storage layers support execution of that choice.

questions.prompt: All pages needed by a query are cached in a disk-oriented DBMS. What follows?
options: The DBMS has permanently become in-memory.
Durability no longer needs persistence.
The schema becomes irrelevant.
This execution can avoid data-page reads while the architecture remains disk-oriented.
questions.explanation: A cached working set changes the I/O of this execution, not the storage architecture or durable-commit requirements.

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly distinguishes workload from storage architecture?
options: OLTP and OLAP describe workloads; disk-oriented and in-memory describe storage designs.
OLTP means RAM and OLAP means HDD.
Column storage prohibits transactions.
RAM is automatically durable.
questions.explanation: Transaction and analytical workload characteristics are separate from the storage tiers and physical layout selected by a DBMS.

questions.prompt: Why is a database update held only in ordinary RAM not automatically durable?
options: RAM cannot hold rows.
Every analytical query modifies data.
Ordinary RAM is volatile.
Indexes cannot reside in RAM.
questions.explanation: Ordinary volatile memory loses its contents on power loss. Durability needs the system's persistence protocol, even for an in-memory working set.

questions.prompt: Updating a department name in three files but forgetting the third illustrates which problem?
options: An error caused only by selecting too few columns
An error caused only by integer formatting
Redundancy leading to inconsistency
An error caused only by a missing sort order
questions.explanation: Multiple copies of the same information can drift apart. The problem is inconsistent data, not the hardware.

questions.prompt: A transfer debits one account and then crashes before crediting the other. What is missing?
options: The ability to sort data by account
The ability to remove duplicate rows
Fast account lookup
Atomic updates
questions.explanation: The two changes must form one unit. Compression or sorting cannot repair an update left half-finished.

questions.prompt: When is code that always treats record[1] as the department name most likely to fail?
options: When the file’s field order changes
When the record count increases but field order stays unchanged
When salaries increase but the schema stays unchanged
When configuration changes the filename but field layout stays unchanged
questions.explanation: The code depends on the physical layout. Moving a field makes it read a value with the wrong meaning.

questions.prompt: Two people edit an old copy of a file and then overwrite each other’s changes. What is the main concern?
options: Removing duplicates from a report
Coordinating concurrent access
Choosing the output sort order
Choosing the columns in a projection
questions.explanation: One person’s work can be lost through an overwrite. Changing number formats does not coordinate their writes.

questions.prompt: What is the drawback of repeating a nonnegative-score rule in many programs?
options: It automatically provides atomicity for multi-file updates
It automatically synchronises all concurrent access
It makes the constraint difficult to change and enforce consistently
It guarantees that the constraint stays consistent across all code versions
questions.explanation: Constraints scattered through application code are difficult to maintain. Their presence does not automatically provide indexes or transactions.

questions.prompt: At which level does a record’s byte offset belong?
options: Logical
View
An instance of business data
Physical
questions.explanation: The physical level describes how data is stored; the logical level describes what the data means.

questions.prompt: At which level does the list of fields name, dept, salary belong?
options: Logical
Physical byte layout
A user-specific restricted view
An instance of one specific record
questions.explanation: A record schema describes the data structure. It does not yet specify offsets or who may see each column.

questions.prompt: A screen hides salaries but displays employee names. Which level does this illustrate?
options: Disk-space allocation
View
Physical level
The complete logical schema of the database
questions.explanation: A view limits what a user sees. Changing disk sectors does not determine which columns are visible.

questions.prompt: What is the aim of data independence?
options: To require every application to know the byte layout
To guarantee that data needs no schema
To reduce higher-level dependence on lower-level changes
To guarantee that data never changes
questions.explanation: The aim is to isolate lower-level details. It does not mean that the database remains unchanged.

questions.prompt: Page storage changes, but a query for book titles remains the same. What does this illustrate?
options: Query logic must depend on every new offset
A physical-layout change necessarily changes business data
Every view must expose all storage details
The benefit of abstraction
questions.explanation: A stable interface can hide physical changes, so the business question need not be rewritten.

questions.prompt: What does a data model provide?
options: Concepts for describing data
Only the tuples currently in a table
A specific schema for exactly one application
One mandatory physical layout
questions.explanation: A model is a system of concepts. The current data is a particular instance.

questions.prompt: How does a schema differ from a model?
options: A schema is always every byte in a file
A schema uses a model to describe a particular dataset
A schema is all the current tuples
A model describes exactly one instance
questions.explanation: One model can support many schemas. A schema is a specific description made using that model.

questions.prompt: What is Book(id,title) best understood as?
options: A complete physical page layout
A record containing two specific values
A relational schema
An instance containing exactly one book
questions.explanation: It names a relation and its attributes without supplying the values for any particular book.

questions.prompt: Which pair consists of data models mentioned in the lecture?
options: LRU and CLOCK
Heap files and sorted files
Selection and projection
Graph and document
questions.explanation: Graph and document models describe ways to model data. The other pairs are system mechanisms or operations.

questions.prompt: Must two applications using the relational model have the same schema?
options: No; each application can describe different relations
Yes; the model fixes every relation name
Yes; the model fixes all current tuples
Yes; the model fixes every field in each application
questions.explanation: A model supplies common concepts. It does not prescribe one schema or one instance.
